title: PhaBOX2: an enhanced web server for discovering and analyzing viral contigs in metagenomic data.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened the only two tables the project distributes, from the PhaBOX GitHub repo: ICTV_classification.csv (8.9 MB, 59,907 rows, 30 columns) and phagcn_prediction.tsv (8.0 MB, 59,907 rows, 7 columns, 59,907 unique IDs). Both are PhaGCN's own taxonomy predictions on ICTV Taxonomy Challenge sequences, with score columns and no true-answer column; 59.5% of rows have no realm call and 100% have no species call. Confirmed by HEAD that the reference database phabox_db_v2_2.zip is a live, login-free 704,676,905-byte download (plus phabox_db_v2.zip 733.4 MB, phabox_db_v2_1.zip 743.0 MB, example_contigs.fa 5.6 MB); I did not download it because it is far over the 50 MB cap, and a ranged peek at its file listing was refused by the server (HTTP 501). Listed the whole GitHub repository tree (57 files): source code plus those two tables, no other data file.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The benchmarking setup and all performance numbers (train on RefSeq genomes released before 2022, 4,062 held-out sequences, fragments of 1,000-10,000 bp; virus identification F1 0.98, genus-level taxonomy F1 0.90, host prediction species-level accuracy 0.77 prokaryotic / 0.71 eukaryotic, lifestyle accuracy 0.98) come from the paper's text only. Supplementary Tables S1-S8, which hold those benchmarks, were not retrievable: the Europe PMC supplementary-files endpoint timed out on two attempts.

a1_downloadable.note: Paper's data availability statement gives only the web server URL (no login), but the code and a 704.7 MB reference database download freely from GitHub releases; verified HTTP 200 and byte size by HEAD.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL, verified in the files. Neither distributed table contains a true label: both hold PhaGCN's predicted taxonomy plus confidence scores. Any real label (true taxonomy, host, lifestyle) would have to be constructed from NCBI RefSeq/ICTV metadata that this paper does not ship.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL, verified. The tables carry only synthetic IDs (ICTVTaxoChallenge_100097 style) and a length column; the input FASTA (ICTV_Challenge.fa) is not in the repository, so every sequence would need fetching elsewhere.

a4_units_stated.note: Not really applicable: columns are categorical taxon names plus 0-1 confidence scores and contig length in base pairs; column meanings are clear from the header.

a5_enough_rows.note: 59,907 rows in each table, verified by reading them, but they are unlabelled predictions, so row count is not the binding constraint.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 704.7 MB compressed reference database, unknown multi-GB unpacked (DIAMOND/MMseqs indexes plus model weights)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Over the project's 50 MB download cap, and the unpacked size could not be checked because the host refused a ranged read of the zip listing. Running the tool itself also assumes a many-core cluster (the paper cites 112 CPU cores).

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No count in the paper to match against the files; the 4,062 held-out test sequences live only in unretrievable Supplementary Tables S1-S8.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL, verified. The taxonomy columns in both shipped tables are PhaGCN model output (the README says they were produced by running phabox2 --task phagcn). Training on them would distil PhaBOX2's own classifier, not learn biology.

existing_models.name: PhaBOX2 itself (bundling PhaMer, PhaGCN, CHERRY/HostG, PhaTYP, PhaVIP)
existing_models.score_and_split: Paper reports virus-identification F1 0.98 on complete genomes, genus-level taxonomy F1 0.90, host species-level accuracy 0.77 (prokaryotic viruses) and 0.71 (eukaryotic DNA viruses), lifestyle accuracy 0.98, on a date-based split: RefSeq genomes before 2022 for training, 4,062 later sequences held out.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: They state that pure DNA-based deep learning is more sensitive on short, uncharacterised fragments, while PhaBOX2 rejects contigs under 3,000 bp or without protein alignment hits; so short and novel contigs are the admitted gap.

existing_models.name: geNomad (Nature Biotechnology 2023)
existing_models.score_and_split: Best overall in a Genome Biology 2024 cross-biome benchmark: Matthews correlation coefficient 95.3% and F1 97.3% for virus classification across contig-length strata.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Benchmark authors note tools recover different, partly non-overlapping viral subsets, so recall on novel viruses remains open.

existing_models.name: VirSorter2
existing_models.score_and_split: Matthews correlation coefficient 81.3%, F1 88.9% in the same Genome Biology 2024 real-world metagenome benchmark; degrades on contigs under 10 kb.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Short-contig performance, because it needs complete protein information.

existing_models.name: ViraLM (Bioinformatics 2024, genome foundation model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to outperform competing identifiers across all contig-length ranges, including short contigs; evaluated on held-out RefSeq-derived fragments.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation to genuinely novel viral lineages.

existing_models.name: iPHoP, CHERRY, PHIST, RaFAH, PHP, DeepHost (host prediction)
existing_models.score_and_split: Compared head-to-head in a Briefings in Bioinformatics 2025 benchmark of 27 virus-host prediction tools on two public benchmark sets, RefSeq-VHDB (database-centric) and MetaHiC-VHDB (metagenomic, host assignment from Hi-C linkage); no tool was universally best, CHERRY and iPHoP were the most broadly robust, PHIST best at exact-match level in cow faecal and human gut data.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Performance is strongly context-dependent and drops on metagenome-derived hosts; no tool is universally optimal.

backbone.name: Nucleotide Transformer / DNABERT-2 / HyenaDNA would fit viral contigs, and ESM-2 would fit viral proteins
backbone.hardware: CPU-feasible for small checkpoints on a few thousand contigs, GPU preferred
backbone.licence: Open weights, but irrelevant here because this paper ships no labelled data to fit a head on

integration.partner_dataset: NCBI Viral RefSeq plus ICTV Master Species List, and GTDB for host taxonomy
integration.join_key: NCBI nucleotide accession and NCBI taxonomy ID
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: The join is possible in principle, but it would be a project built on RefSeq and ICTV rather than on anything this paper contributes, since the paper distributes no accession-keyed measurements of its own.

controls.positive_control: None available in this paper's files; the usual one (recover known Caudoviricetes genus assignments) requires ICTV labels fetched elsewhere.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling would be runnable only after labels were obtained from an external source.
controls.external_validation: RefSeq-VHDB and MetaHiC-VHDB from the 2025 Briefings in Bioinformatics host-prediction benchmark exist and are independent, but again belong to other authors, not to this paper.

honest_claim_h3: Nothing can be honestly claimed from this paper's own files, because the only tables it distributes are 59,907 rows of its own classifier's predictions with no ground truth and no sequences attached.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a viral DNA fragment from an environmental sample to predict its taxonomy, its host bacterium and its lifestyle.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would train on viral contigs (assembled DNA fragments from mixed-community sequencing) paired with curated taxonomy and host labels. This paper supplies 59,907 rows of predictions, verified by opening the files, and zero labelled examples.
plain_idea.predict: Taxonomic rank assignments (family, genus), the host organism, and whether the virus is temperate or virulent. The true answers would come from ICTV expert curation and from the host organism recorded at isolation, neither of which is in the paper's files.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Viral ecologists sifting metagenomes need host calls to know which bacteria a virus controls; but this question is already served by many open tools, so the value here would be marginal.

more_or_better_data.why: The paper contributes no new measurements at all: its models are retrained on NCBI Viral RefSeq, the same public source geNomad, VirSorter2, ViraLM and iPHoP already use. We would have no data the incumbents lack.

confidence_score.why: There are no replicate measurements to estimate noise, and PhaBOX2 already emits per-rank confidence scores (I saw the Realm_score through Genus_score columns), so calibrated confidence is not an open gap we could fill.

models_beatable.why: The incumbents are recent (geNomad 2023, ViraLM 2024, PhaBOX2 2026) and already evaluated on honest splits: a date-based split here, and in the November 2025 Briefings in Bioinformatics study, 27 host-prediction tools on two independent benchmark sets.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The first condition fails outright: this paper provides no labelled data that the baselines did not already see, so our model would see strictly less, not more.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: fine-tune a DNA language model (for example DNABERT-2 or Nucleotide Transformer) on viral contigs to predict genus and bacterial host, with a date-based split. It dies here because this paper ships no labels and no sequences, and the field already contains several open, honestly benchmarked models.

effort.compute_note: Only the 704.7 MB compressed reference database size is measured (HEAD request); unpacked size, RAM and runtime could not be estimated because the archive exceeds the download cap and a ranged listing was refused.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open the two tables in the repository and look for a ground-truth column. Five minutes; there is none, only predicted taxonomy with confidence scores.

verdict_reason: Fails A2 and A8, verified in the files. PhaBOX2 is a web-server paper whose data availability statement is a URL: the only tabular data it distributes are 59,907 rows of its own PhaGCN classifier's taxonomy predictions on ICTV Challenge sequences, with no true labels, no sequences and 59.5% of rows unclassified even at realm level. Training on that distils the tool rather than learning biology. A3 also fails (inputs absent) and A6 is doubtful (704.7 MB database, cluster-scale tooling). Separately, the field is saturated: geNomad, VirSorter2, ViraLM for identification and iPHoP, CHERRY, PHIST for host prediction are all open and already benchmarked honestly, including a 27-tool comparison in late 2025.
